item.text: {"question_id":"4B.5","answer":"For the 2023 period, appointments and personnel decisions did not clearly preserve politically neutral institutions. Tshisekedi’s presidential ordinances revoked, compulsorily retired, dismissed, reassigned, and appointed civilian and military magistrates across senior courts, prosecutors’ offices, appellate courts, trial courts, and military courts; the supplied record gives no individual reasons, selection criteria, qualifications, or tenure safeguards. [BATCH-0015-E006, BATCH-0019-E005, BATCH-0019-E006] He also appointed or reconfirmed managers and board chairs across numerous public enterprises and regulatory bodies, reshuffled the cabinet, and presided over a newly appointed Gécamines leadership team, but the records do not establish whether these appointments were merit-based, partisan, or effective. [BATCH-0008-E014, BATCH-0009-E003, BATCH-0018-E004] The adverse evidence is stronger at the institutional-perception level: ACLED reported concerns that CENI was politically close to the government and that Denis Kadima was viewed by critics as close to Tshisekedi, while Human Rights Watch described the CENI and Constitutional Court as perceived to be politicized and favoring the authorities. [BATCH-0010-E020, BATCH-0028-E018] The New York Review of Books reported that Tshisekedi moved to place sympathetic judges in the judiciary and quoted an allegation that the Constitutional Court had been stacked with people from his ethnic group; these remain reported allegations rather than adjudicated findings. [BATCH-0028-E021] Formal administrative safeguards existed: budget-governance rules required program objectives, indicators, reporting, internal controls, independent and objective internal audit, audit committees, and external competent participation, while UNDP and ILO supported magistrate, police, and labor-inspector recruitment or training. [BATCH-0029-E004, BATCH-0029-E005, BATCH-0009-E004, BATCH-0023-E017] However, those provisions and capacity-building activities do not demonstrate neutral personnel practice or implementation. Presidential rhetoric emphasized loyalty to the nation rather than personal interests in the military, and a thesis characterized his speeches as reinforcing presidential authority and power; neither establishes systematic loyalty tests or a personality cult. [BATCH-0019-E010, BATCH-0012-R09-E002] Attribution is strongest for the presidential ordinances and appointments. Broader politicization, patronage, ethnic capture, and institutional dysfunction remain partly inferential, perception-based, or institution-level, so the supplied evidence supports substantial neutrality risks but not a conclusive finding of systematic loyalty tests or personalist
